## Run 46 Summary — Backend API QA

**Result: All endpoints tested, 0 broken, 0 fixes needed (6th consecutive converged run).**

I re-ran the full standing probe suite against the live API on port 3001 and added direct happy-path + security checks:

| Surface | Result |
|---|---|
| 63 uncovered GET routes | 62 <500, 1 intentional 503, **0 unintentional 5xx** |
| Negative-case gaps (bad UUIDs, empty/malformed bodies) | 46×400, 19×404 — graceful, no crashes |
| Edge (malformed JSON, SQL injection, bad auth) | 400/401/empty-result, **0 5xx** |
| Type-fuzz, patch/delete, main API probes | all clean |
| Happy-path PATCH `/crm/leads/:id`, `/crm/invoices/:id` | **200** (valid writes work, not just rejections) |
| Tenant isolation | foreign estimate GET/PATCH/PDF → **404**; `tenant_id` query/body/header injection **ignored**, returns own-tenant data only |

The only non-2xx-by-design responses are intentional: skip-trace 503 (no `TRACERFY_API_KEY`, per the zero-paid-API charter) and auth 429 (rate-limiter). Per the charter, nothing was broken, so nothing was changed.

**Notable finding (tooling, not the app):** I traced the long-recurring "mass 401" symptom in the probes to a Bash↔Node path mismatch — `curl > /tmp/qa-token.txt` (Git-Bash's `/tmp`) doesn't land where Node reads it (`C:\tmp`), so probes ran on a stale token and every authenticated route returned `401 "Invalid or expired token"`. This is what made past runs look like an auth outage. Fixed by minting through Node's `fs.writeFileSync`, and documented the correct command at the top of `overnight_resume.md`.

**Deliverables:**
- `C:\tmp\api-test-results.txt` — full results table
- Commit `8d12947` — refreshed probe snapshots + run notes
- Resume + MEMORY.md updated; next-run guidance points away from the (converged) backend toward the untouched frontend gaps (tablet 768px sweep, a11y/axe-core, keyboard nav).
